mission: Build an evidence-traceable encyclopedia of education policy: goals, rights, institutions, instruments, implementation, consequences and controversies. UNESCO labels anchor discovery, not the exhaustive editorial scope or proof of factual claims.
core_question: How are educational goals translated into public decisions, legal rights, resources, institutions and measurable outcomes, under what circumstances and with what evidence?

grain.future_split_rule: Split only for distinct semantic ownership or independently governed evidence, not an arbitrary number of pages.

owned_subjects: education-policy concepts and their disambiguated meanings
policy goals and their explicit normative context
legal and institutional education-policy arrangements, when sourced
policy instruments, implementation responsibilities, resource allocation and monitoring
evidence-qualified outcomes, trade-offs and unresolved disputes
excluded_subjects: learning psychology, classroom pedagogy and teaching methods except policy implications
full legal interpretation of constitutions, treaties and court rulings beyond education-policy relevance
general macroeconomic policy and noneducation public finance
complete histories of individual schools, persons or ministries
country-level data without source/date/jurisdiction or a demonstrable education-policy link
encyclopedic assertion inferred from a UNESCO label, Wikidata candidate match or AI suggestion alone

facet_taxonomy.label: Rights, duties and normative frameworks
prompts: What is the legal jurisdiction and date?

facet_taxonomy.label: Policy design, planning and reform
prompts: How does implementation differ from adoption?

facet_taxonomy.label: Financing and allocation
prompts: What is allocated and according to which rule?

facet_taxonomy.label: Teachers and education workforce policy
prompts: What evidence concerns delivery or outcomes?

facet_taxonomy.label: System standards and educational pathways
prompts: What standards or pathways are governed?
What is outside policy and belongs to pedagogy?

facet_taxonomy.label: Monitoring, outcomes and causal evidence
prompts: Does evidence establish causation or association?
What is the year and population?

facet_taxonomy.label: Comparative, historical and international policy
prompts: Which jurisdictions and time periods are compared?

controlled_vocabulary.source: UNESCO SKOS thesaurus snapshot in original Factory RUN
controlled_vocabulary.rule: Every original member and stable UNESCO URI is retained; keywords are research/query facets, not replacements for source labels.
controlled_vocabulary.membership: Use actual 41 imported concepts as baseline, never infer ids from keywords.
controlled_vocabulary.non_members: May be represented as evidence contexts or cross-branch links; new owned entities require review.

vocabulary_only: UNESCO Thesaurus / SKOS labels, membership and relations

law_or_right: primary treaty, statute, regulation or official legal instrument, dated and jurisdiction-specific
statistic: UNESCO UIS or other primary statistical producer with series definition, year and coverage
policy_action: official policy document or implementation record, plus independent evaluation where available
causal_effect: methodologically appropriate peer-reviewed study or credible evaluation, with limitations
history: dated primary records and reliable historical scholarship

candidate_sources: UNESCO and UNESCO Institute for Statistics
source_policy.wikidata: Candidate identifiers and lead generation only until individually checked; raw P statements are not encyclopedic truth.

quality_gates.G0: Lock the original branch and inspect its actual 41 seed concepts, IDs and relations.
quality_gates.G1: Approve scope and semantic ownership; keep a design-only Kristal without promoted assertions.
quality_gates.G2: Create and review one comprehensive article for concept10, with independently verifiable claims and source locators.
quality_gates.G3: Review a small contrasting sample of concepts and test cross-branch relationships before scaling.
quality_gates.G4: Process all 41 seed concepts; publish only after structural, factual, licensing and editorial qualification.
